claims.text: Chemical short-range order in high-entropy alloys creates a heterogeneous lattice strain field.
The heterogeneous lattice strain field induces turbulent dislocation flow and vortex structures.
Dislocation vortices act both as sources for dislocation multiplication and as traps that pin moving dislocations.
The dual source-and-trap behavior improves both strength and ductility.
The proposed initial material is a BCC multi-principal element alloy with significant chemical short-range order and lattice distortion.
Heat treatments or compositional modifications can controllably vary chemical short-range order while other processing parameters are held constant.
Dynamic tests at controlled strain rates and temperatures can be conducted in a regime where dislocation activity is resolvable.
Spatially variable chemically induced strain causes dislocations to accelerate and decelerate irregularly.
A strongly short-range-ordered MPEA will exhibit higher strain peaks than a minimally ordered baseline.
A strongly short-range-ordered MPEA will exhibit broader strain wavelengths than a minimally ordered baseline.
A strongly short-range-ordered MPEA will show dislocation vortex structures.
A strongly short-range-ordered MPEA will have a better strength-ductility balance than a minimally ordered baseline.
Minimizing chemical short-range order also minimizes the associated lattice distortions.
The proposed mechanism applies within BCC multi-principal element alloys under dynamic mechanical loading.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to regimes where dislocation dynamics dominate plastic deformation.
The mechanism may not operate in other crystal structures or under conditions dominated by other deformation mechanisms.
The source-versus-trap interplay and its mechanical effects over temperature and strain-rate ranges have not been fully quantified.
Failure to observe statistically significant differences in vortices, strain characteristics, or strength-ductility balance between high- and low-order samples would falsify the mechanism.
